text: Explain why a city might plant trees along residential streets. Give a balanced explanation for a general reader. Street trees can provide shade, reduce summer heat and make walking more pleasant. Their roots and maintenance needs must also be considered. A suitable species should match the available space and local climate. Planting decisions work best when residents and maintenance crews are consulted before the trees arrive.

Describe how a community library could welcome first-time visitors. Use clear practical language without assuming familiarity with library services. A visible information desk can help people find books and understand borrowing rules. Staff can explain how to obtain a library card. Quiet areas, accessible signs and an easy map reduce confusion. Activities should be advertised both online and at the entrance.

Explain how to organize a small neighborhood cleanup. Begin with planning and finish with follow-up. Choose a safe public location and ask the relevant owner for permission. Provide gloves, bags and clear instructions about hazardous waste. Divide volunteers into small teams and arrange collection of the filled bags. Afterward, thank participants and record what equipment would help at the next event.

Write a short explanation of why meeting agendas are useful. Keep the tone neutral and practical. An agenda lets participants prepare information before a meeting begins. It also helps the group decide which questions require a decision and which only need an update. Allocating time to each topic can prevent one issue from consuming the whole session. Unfinished questions should receive a clear follow-up owner.

Solve the equation 3x + 7 = 22 and explain each operation. Subtract 7 from both sides to obtain 3x = 15. Divide both sides by 3, giving x = 5. Substituting the value into the original expression gives 3 times 5 plus 7, which equals 22. The check confirms that the operations preserved the equation and that the solution satisfies it.

Find the area of a rectangle whose length is 12 centimeters and width is 7 centimeters. The area of a rectangle is the product of its length and width. Multiplying 12 by 7 gives 84. Therefore the area is 84 square centimeters. The unit is squared because the calculation measures a two-dimensional region rather than a distance around the boundary.

Calculate the mean of the five numbers 4, 6, 8, 10 and 12. First add the numbers to get a total of 40. There are five observations, so divide the total by 5. The arithmetic mean is 8. This value is also the middle of the evenly spaced sequence, which gives a separate way to check the answer.

A bag contains three red balls and two blue balls. Find the probability of drawing a red ball when every ball is equally likely to be chosen. There are five balls in total, and three of them satisfy the event. The probability is therefore 3 divided by 5, or 0.6. This can also be written as 60 percent for a single draw.

Explain how a museum could make an exhibition easier to navigate. Offer practical suggestions for visitors with different needs. The entrance should state what the exhibition covers and how long a visit usually takes. A consistent sign system can identify each section. Seating and accessible routes let visitors choose their own pace. Short descriptions should be readable without requiring everyone to use a phone.

Describe a sensible way to introduce a shared kitchen rota in an office. Explain the goal without blaming particular people. Start by listing the small tasks that need regular attention, such as wiping surfaces and emptying bins. Ask colleagues which schedule would be practical. Make responsibilities visible and easy to exchange. Review the arrangement after a few weeks and adjust tasks that were underestimated.

A train travels 150 kilometers in two and a half hours. Calculate its average speed and explain the units. Average speed is distance divided by elapsed time. Dividing 150 kilometers by 2.5 hours gives 60 kilometers per hour. This describes the average over the whole trip, not the speed at every instant. Stops and faster sections can both contribute to the same average.

Find the total cost of three notebooks priced at four dollars each and two pens priced at one dollar each. First multiply the notebook price by the number purchased to get twelve dollars. The pens cost two dollars together. Adding the two subtotals gives fourteen dollars. This calculation assumes that the listed prices already include any taxes and that no discount is applied.
